Hi Alicia / Tom  great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today's discovery call: 

Recap (what we heard)
- NimbusAI is planning a public launch of the real-time assistance feature in Q3; primary concerns are uptime during peak events, predictable rate limits for burst traffic, and behavior during multi-region failover.
- You currently evaluate both hyperscaler managed endpoints and third-party inference APIs; you want apples-to-apples tests on uptime, error behavior under load, and failover transparency.
- Success criteria for Nimbus: 99.95% availability for production traffic, bounded error budget for 5xx/timeout errors, and sub-100ms P95 latency for median requests at typical payload sizes.

Action items / proposed next steps
1) Redwood will share an SLO comparison doc and a proposed test plan (attached). The doc maps our Dedicated and Hosted guarantees against typical hyperscaler behaviors.
2) Run a 48-hour reliability & failover test: sustained baseline traffic + one controlled AZ/region failover window and a short DDoS-like burst to exercise rate limiting and error-budget behavior.
3) Technical deep-dive with Jordan (solutions) to validate integration details and to define the exact payloads and routing policies. Suggested slots: Thu/Fri this week.
4) Share SOC2 & network diagrams (we flagged SOC2 in the call); Marissa will coordinate if you want a security-specific review.

Attachments: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf (PDF), proposed-test-plan.xlsx (Excel)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4571

Where we think Redwood can help vs hyperscalers (short)
- Predictable throughput: Dedicated GPU pools and configurable burst capacity for steadier error budgets.
- Failover behavior: Smart routing with automatic fallback to compatible model variants (multi-tier) instead of opaque instance restarts.
- Cost controls: batching/caching primitives reduce per-token cost for long-tail workloads.

Questions for you before we schedule the deep-dive:
- Which region(s) do you want in-scope for the failover test?
- Any strict IP allowlist / network constraints we should be aware of up front?

Thanks  I attached the SLO comparison and proposed test plan. Jordan/Marissa standing by for the deep-dive.

Alicia  great questions, answered inline below. I'm also pasting a concise comparison so your engineering team can quickly review.

On Wed, Mar 18, 2026 at 10:05 AM Alicia Gomez <alicia@NimbusAI.com> wrote:
> For rate limits, do you have hard per-second RPS caps per API key for Hosted vs Dedicated, or is it enforced as token throughput?

Short answer: Both. Details:
- Hosted API: default per-API-key rate limits are token-based and request-based. Typical default is 1200 token/s per key with a soft burst allowance; we can provision custom tokens/s and hard RPS caps for customers on dedicated plans.
- Dedicated: you get reserved capacity (GPU pools) and we expose throughput units that map to predictable RPS and token/s for the pinned model. For deal planning we can provide a capacity table that maps expected RPS to reserved pool sizes.

> How do you define "error budget" operationally?

We define the error budget as a blended metric: % of successful requests (2xx) at the configured latency SLO (e.g., P95 <= 100ms). Operationally: error_budget_burn = 1 - (successful_requests_within_latency / total_requests). We track 5xx spikes separately as immediate incidents. For Hosted customers we publish a 99.9% availability SLO for API uptime; Dedicated customers can contract 99.95% SLA with on-call escalation and quarterly reviews.

Concise comparison vs typical hyperscaler managed endpoints:
- Hyperscalers
  - Pros: mature infra, global regions, integrated billing.
  - Cons: often opaque failover behavior, cold-start variability for inference, higher incremental cost for many short requests, less tailored KV cache/batching optimizations out-of-the-box.

- Redwood (how we differ)
  - Dedicated GPU pools and predictable throughput -> steadier error budget consumption under bursty traffic.
  - Smart routing & multi-variant fallback -> graceful degradation to smaller/compatible models rather than hard failures.
  - Built-in prefix/KV caching and batching -> reduces both latency and downstream token cost for conversational workloads.
  - Rollouts and traceable evals -> we can tie SLO regressions to specific model versions and roll back automatically.

Proposed reliability & failover test plan (high level)
1) Baseline run (24h) at nominal traffic pattern to collect P95/P99 latency and baseline 5xx rate.
2) Burst test: 15-minute ramp to 4x baseline to observe rate limiting and spike behavior.
3) Failover test: shift 60% of traffic to a second region over 10 minutes, then simulate an instance/availability failure in the primary region and measure error budget burn and recovery time.
4) Post-test analysis: compare error budget burn against target SLA, inspect traces for increased tail latency, and run deterministic retry tests.

I'll attach the more detailed test plan (proposed-test-plan.xlsx) and a short SLO comparison PDF with our Hosted vs Dedicated numbers and recommended thresholds. Jordan, can you join the deep-dive and confirm any integration blockers we should call out? Marissa, can you surface SOC2 docs if Nimbus wants them before the tech call?

Suggested deep-dive: Thu 3/19 10:00 PT works for us. I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Ben
